newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Denktash to visit Turkey ahead of U.N. talks.
newsitem.headline: Denktash to visit Turkey ahead of U.N. talks.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash said on Thursday he would meet Turkish leaders in Ankara this week ahead of U.N.-sponsored talks with Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides.
"There is a new government in Turkey and I am glad I will have the opportunity for exchanging views with all concerned," Denktash told Reuters. He is due in Turkey on Friday.

He said he would definitely attend the talks with Clerides in the United States despite threatening this week to pull out if any document is put on the table before he has been informed of its contents.

The two rival leaders are to meet in New York from July 9 to 13 in a tentative bid to end the division of Cyprus. The island has been split since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a Greek Cypriot coup backed by Athens.
"The Cyprus problem is a very sensitive national problem in Turkey and is always treated in a non-partisan way. It is the only problem on which all parties act and decide unanimously," Denktash said.
Denktash heads a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state that is recognised only by Ankara. Clerides leads the Greek Cypriot administration, regarded abroad as the island's only government.
He will meet President Suleyman Demirel, Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz, Foreign Minister Ismail Cem and Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit during his one-day visit.
Former prime minister Ecevit ordered the 1974 invasion and is still regarded as a hawk on the Cyprus issue.

He is back in office after 18 years in opposition thanks to the establishment this week of a secularist coalition to replace the Islamist-led government of prime minister Necemttin Erbakan, who resigned last month.
